draft.title: Mountains, sea and city-states
card: Greece is a land of mountains, with little flat farmland. Mountains and rough ground made travel by land slow and hard.
a city-state. Because the land was split up, Greek communities grew apart, and each polis had its own government and laws.
Greece also has a very long coast, with many bays and islands. No place in Greece is far from the sea.
Travel by sea was often easier than by land. Many Greeks became sailors and traders, and they carried goods and ideas to other lands.
draft.remember: Mountains kept Greek communities apart as city-states. The sea linked them to the wider world.

a.q: Why did Greece develop many separate city-states instead of one united country?
opts: Mountains made land travel hard and kept communities apart
The sea cut Greece off from all other lands and peoples
Each polis was forced to have its own government by law
Greece had too little coast for its people to trade by sea
a.why: Mountains and rough ground made travel between communities slow, so each grew apart with its own government. The sea did not isolate Greece. Its long coast helped people travel and trade.
a.clue: Think about what made travelling over land difficult.

b.q: Nikos lives in a village on a Greek island in ancient times. He wants to sell olive oil to people far away. How is he most likely to travel?
opts: By boat, because sea travel was often easier than land
By road, because Greece had flat land and easy roads
He would not travel, because the sea kept Greeks apart
By road, because every polis shared one government
b.why: Greece has a long coast and many islands, and sea travel was often easier than crossing mountains. That is why many Greeks became sailors and traders. The sea did not keep Greeks apart.
b.clue: Which way of travelling suited a land of islands and mountains?

a.best: Mountains made land travel hard and kept communities apart

b.best: By boat, because sea travel was often easier than land
